questions.question: In the OR study cycle, which stage comes directly after the solution of the mathematical model?
options: Validation of the model and its solution
Implementation of the solution in practice
Formulation of the mathematical model
Choice of the assumed representation

questions.question: What does the validation stage of the OR study cycle check?
options: Whether the software solved the model without any arithmetic errors
Whether the model and its solution adequately represent the real problem
Whether the solution is optimal for the model exactly as it was stated
Whether all the numbers were typed into the model exactly as supplied

questions.question: A team studying lecture scheduling decides which features of the real situation to include, for example that rooms have capacities, and which to ignore, for example teachers' room preferences. Which stage of the OR study cycle is this?
options: The assumed representation of the situation
The mathematical model, written as equations
The validation of the model and its solution
The implementation of the recommended plan

questions.question: A delivery model is solved correctly, yet the planners reject its recommended routes as unworkable. In terms of the OR study cycle, what is the most likely cause?
options: The software made an arithmetic error in solving the model
The model's assumptions omit a feature essential in practice
The model used too much data for the planners to follow it
The model's objective was a linear function of its variables

questions.question: A detailed traffic model would need the number of cars on every street for every hour, and these counts cannot be obtained. What does the OR study cycle imply for this model?
options: It can be used by setting the missing counts to zero
It can be used with guessed counts, as validation will correct them
It cannot be used as planned; it must suit obtainable data
It should be used anyway, as more detail gives better plans

questions.question: After a timetable model has been solved, the planners compare its recommended timetable with last year's timetable and ask teaching staff whether it is workable. Which stage of the OR study cycle is this?
options: Implementation of the recommended timetable
Validation of the model and of its solution
Solution of the mathematical timetable model
Formulation of the mathematical model itself

questions.question: A team studying lecture scheduling has agreed to treat each room as having a fixed capacity and to ignore teachers' preferences. It now writes, for every room and hour, the inequality 'students assigned $\le$ capacity'. Which stage of the OR study cycle is this writing?
options: The assumed representation of the situation
The validation of the model and its solution
The solution of the model by a computation
The mathematical model built from the representation

questions.question: A route model approximates travel by straight lines. Validation shows that a river crossed by only one bridge makes the recommended routes much longer in reality. To which stage of the OR study cycle should the team return?
options: The solution stage, to solve the same model again
Implementation, to correct routes while driving
Validation, to repeat the check on more of the routes
The assumed representation, to include the roads

questions.question: A route model that uses one travel time per road is extended with time-dependent traffic, a different travel time for each hour. What is the likely effect, according to the OR study cycle?
options: More realism at no extra cost, since the roads are unchanged
Less data needed, since the times are more exact
More realism, but more data to collect and harder solving
Easier solving, since exact times narrow the choice of routes

questions.question: A team has built a staffing model, solved it, and the managers have confirmed in validation that its plan is workable. Which stage of the OR study cycle remains?
options: Implementation, putting the plan into practice
A second validation of the already validated plan
A new formulation of the mathematical model
A new collection of data for the same model

questions.question: Why does the OR study cycle place validation before implementation rather than after it?
options: The order is arbitrary, as both checks reach the same verdict
Implementation needs validated data; validation needs none
Inadequate assumptions get revised before acting on a plan
Validation only checks the software, so it must come first

questions.question: A consultant builds a model, computes its optimal solution, hands it over and leaves before anyone checks it against practice. What does the OR study cycle say about this?
options: The work is complete; an optimal model solution is the result
The work is unfinished; validation belongs to the same process
The work is complete if the consultant's software is reliable
Validation is optional and can be left to the client later on

questions.question: A team argues that the most detailed model it can write is always the best choice. Why is this not true in the OR study cycle?
options: The simplest possible model is always the better choice instead
Detail cannot improve realism, since every model simplifies
A more detailed model always gives the same decision as a simple one
Detail raises data needs and solving effort, offsetting realism

questions.question: A depot is at $(0,0)$ and two candidate warehouses at $P=(3,4)$ and $Q=(6,0)$, in km. A model with straight-line distances picks the nearer warehouse; in reality roads run only east-west and north-south. What does validation reveal?
options: The model picks Q (6 km), which is also nearer by road (6 vs 7 km)
The model picks P (5 km), but Q is nearer by road (6 vs 7 km)
The model picks P (5 km), which is also nearer by road (5 vs 6 km)
Both warehouses are equally near, by straight line and by road alike

questions.question: A route model for a depot and 9 customers uses one travel time per pair of locations, the same in both directions. A more detailed version uses a separate travel time for each of 12 periods of the day. How many travel times must be collected for the detailed version?
options: 540 travel times
45 travel times
108 travel times
1080 travel times

questions.question: To validate a cost model, three past plans are evaluated. The model predicted costs 100, 110 and 120 for plans A, B and C; the actual costs were 130, 115 and 125. What does this comparison show?
options: The model is adequate, since its errors average out over the three plans
The model is adequate, since it underestimates every plan by the same amount
The model is adequate, since plan A was cheapest in both predictions and reality
The model ranks A cheapest, yet B was cheapest; a cost A incurs is missing

questions.question: A production model reproduces last year's actual cost exactly for the plan the firm actually used. Does this show that the model is adequate for choosing a new plan?
options: Yes; reproducing an actual cost proves the model is adequate
Yes, as long as the reproduction is exact to the last euro
No; other plans may use features that the model gets wrong
No; a model is adequate only if it reproduces every past plan exactly

questions.question: A team's mathematical model describes the situation well, but solving it takes several weeks while the decision is due in two days. Which response fits the OR study cycle?
options: Implement the best plan found so far without validating it
Collect more detailed data so that the model solves faster
Skip the validation stage to make up for the lost time
Return to the representation; remove detail that slows it

questions.question: A route model ignores traffic. Validation shows that morning traffic doubles some travel times, but all deliveries take place between 13:00 and 15:00, when actual times match the model to within 2%. Should time-dependent traffic be added?
options: Yes; adding detail always makes the model more adequate
Yes; morning traffic doubles some times, so it must enter
No; for the decision taken, the simpler model is adequate
No; the 2% deviation should be removed before anything else is added

questions.question: A model picks the supplier with the lowest unit price: A (10 per unit), B (11) or C (12). Validation reveals a fixed fee per order: 250 for A, 50 for B, 0 for C. For which order sizes $q$ is the price-only model's choice also cheapest in reality?
options: Only for orders of more than 200 units
For every order size, as fees are small
Only for orders of more than 125 units
Only for orders of fewer than 200 units
